name: Adjacent Clause Signs Can Change Forbidden-pc-Minor Status
statement: There are four 1188-concept ample classes in dimension twenty-six and VC dimension five with a common shadow, whose signed presentations vary over a square of adjacent signs at one clause. Exactly one is a pc-minimal obstruction to dismantlable ampleness; the other three peel, and every proper pc-minor of all four peels. Adding one common root-square concept gives four 1189-concept two-connected classes with the same conclusions.
proof: Glue each 900-concept square pivot at its root to a fresh fixed rooted factor. The negative choice is the wedge of two rooted factors and hence forbidden; each positive choice peels its first block to the root and then clears the fixed block. All new cross-block clauses are common, so the unique varying clause persists. Completing the same root square on all four sides preserves the signs; the square-completed rooted-block theorem makes the negative member forbidden, while the common tip is a first corner on the positive sides. It also joins the two blocks after root deletion, proving two-connectivity. Forbidden minimality and positive pc-minor closure give the proper-minor claims.
